name: Zuiderpark
wikipediaExtract: The Zuiderpark is a city park in The Hague and also one of its wijken. It is part of the Escamp district and borders Moerwijk, Morgenstond, Leyenburg and Rustenburg-Oostbroek.

name: Willemspark
wikipediaExtract: The Willemspark (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈʋɪləmsˌpɑr(ə)k]; lit. 'William's Park') is a neighbourhood in the Centrum district of The Hague, Netherlands. It has 1,393 inhabitants (as of 1 January 2013) and covers an area of 34.6 hectares (0.134 sq mi). It is bordered by the Zeestraat to the south-east, the Scheveningseveer, the Mauritskade and the Dr. Kuyperstraat...

name: Leidschenveen-Ypenburg
wikipediaExtract: Leidschenveen-Ypenburg (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈlɛitsə(ɱ)ˌveːn ˈipə(m)ˌbʏr(ə)x]) is a Vinex-location and district of The Hague, located in the southeast. It is geographically connected to the main body of the city by only a narrow corridor. name: Scheveningen
imageAttribution: Wikimedia Commons: 00 8652 Seebad Scheveningen - Den Haag (NL).jpg
wikipediaExtract: Scheveningen (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈsxeːvənɪŋə(n)] ) is one of the eight districts of The Hague, Netherlands, as well as a subdistrict (wijk) of that city. Scheveningen is a modern seaside resort with a long, sandy beach, an esplanade, a pier, and a lighthouse. The beach is popular for water sports such as windsurfing and kiteboarding. name: Haagse Hout
wikipediaExtract: Haagse Hout (Dutch pronunciation: [ˌɦaːxsə ˈɦʌut]; lit. 'Woods of The Hague') is one of the eight districts of The Hague. This area was originally called Die Haghe Houte, which later became the current Haagse Hout. The district has 50,693 residents as of 1 January 2026. It is located in the north-east of the city, bordering Wassenaar to the north and Leidschendam...

name: Groente- en Fruitmarkt
wikipediaExtract: The Groente- en Fruitmarkt ('fruit and vegetable market') is a wijk of The Hague with a single neighbourhood of the same name. It borders Laakkwartier en Spoorwijk, Moerwijk, Transvaalkwartier and the Schilderswijk.

name: Laak
wikipediaExtract: Laak (Dutch pronunciation: [laːk]) is district of The Hague, Netherlands. With a population of 48,862 and an area of 4.3 square kilometres (1.7 sq mi), it is the smallest and least populous of the city's eight districts. The district is officially divided into three neighbourhoods: Laakkwartier, Spoorwijk and Binckhorst. The Hague University of Applied Sciences...

name: Segbroek
wikipediaExtract: Segbroek (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈsɛɣbruk]) is one of eight districts of The Hague in the Netherlands. The district was established by the city in 1988. It has a total area of 7.19 square kilometres (2.78 sq mi) and a population of 62,828 as of 1 January 2026. Segbroek is divided into five neighbourhoods: Bomen- en Bloemenbuurt, Regentessekwartier, Valkenboskwartier...

name: Centrum
imageAttribution: Wikimedia Commons: Den Haag Centrum nieuwe architectuur.jpg
wikipediaExtract: The City Center of The Hague (Dutch: Centrum) is the oldest and, with a population of 110,237 inhabitants (as of 1 January 2026), the second largest of The Hague's eight districts, consisting of nine neighbourhoods. Two railways stations can be found in the city center: Den Haag Centraal and Den Haag Hollands Spoor.

name: Rustenburg en Oostbroek
wikipediaExtract: Rustenburg-Oostbroek (informally Rustenburg en Oostbroek) is a wijk in The Hague's Escamp district, bounded by the Soestdijksekade, the De La Reyweg and the Loosduinsekade, with about 19,000 inhabitants.

name: Transvaalkwartier
wikipediaExtract: The Transvaalkwartier is a wijk south-west of the centre of The Hague, built between 1900 and 1935. The Haagse Markt, which gives the neighbourhood an international feel, moved here in 1938.

name: Leyenburg
wikipediaExtract: Leyenburg is a wijk in the south-west of The Hague, in the Escamp district, and home to the Leyweg site of the HagaZiekenhuis hospital.

name: Loosduinen

Within the district there is also a neighbourhood (Dutch:wijk) called 'Loosduinen'.

name: Morgenstond
wikipediaExtract: Morgenstond (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈmɔrɣə(n)ˌstɔnt], literally Morning or Dawn) is a 'wijk' in the south of The Hague in the Escamp 'stadsdeel'. Morgenstond was built during the early 50s and borders Bouwlust and Vrederust in the west, Leyenburg and Houtwijk in the north, Moerwijk and Zuiderpark in the east and Wateringse Veld in the south. name: Moerwijk
wikipediaExtract: Moerwijk is a wijk of The Hague in the Escamp district. It was built shortly before and after the Second World War to an urban design by Willem Dudok.

name: Escamp
wikipediaExtract: Escamp (Dutch pronunciation: [ˈɛskɑmp]) is a district of The Hague, Netherlands, built largely after the Second World War, on the 15th century Eskamppolders. With the addition of the Vinex neighbourhood Wateringse Veld, Escamp is the most populous district of the city; as of 1 January 2026, it had 132,579 inhabitants. name: Wateringse Veld
wikipediaExtract: Wateringse Veld is a residential area in The Hague and one of its three Vinex sites: between 1996 and 2012, 7,500 homes were built on the former Wateringse Veld polders. It is part of the Escamp district and borders Bouwlust en Vrederust, Morgenstond and Rijswijk.
